module purpose: neorv32_twd is a bus-configured serial-line interface that stores control bits, samples twd_sda_i and twd_scl_i, detects start/stop and clock edges, compares an incoming 7-bit address against a programmed address, writes received bytes into an RX-side buffer sub-unit, shifts response bytes from a TX-side buffer sub-unit or a stored backup byte onto twd_sda_o, and reports status and interrupts. It also exports the enable state on clkgen_en_o.

use-case flows.value: control settings written into stored control bits: enable, clear requests, sample-clock select, 7-bit device address, interrupt enables, dummy-data enable, and response-suppression setting
a transmit byte staged from the bus into the TX-side buffer input
a detected serial start event begins engine processing
external serial lines are synchronized and turned into qualified rise/fall/start/stop events
response is suppressed after an address match when the stored suppression setting is active and the `tx_fifo.free = '0'` condition holds
addressed serial bytes are received or transmitted, with RX writes and TX reads coordinated by the engine state machine
interrupt request generated from enabled RX/TX status conditions
stored control bits, live status bits, and received-byte data returned on a bus read
control state, sampling state, engine state, outputs, backup byte, and interrupt output forced to known values while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: Configured by `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` (line 159), this stored bit is read back at line 172, copied to `clkgen_en_o` at line 198, clears both buffer sub-units when low (lines 230 and 281), gates interrupt generation (line 293), gates sampling validity (lines 315-317), and starts or aborts the serial engine (lines 381, 389, 397, 421, 434 and 465). Integrity is established because these implemented flows change directly if the stored enable is wrong; availability is established because sampling and engine operation only proceed while it remains asserted.

`ctrl.device_addr` and `ctrl.hide_read` are stored from bus writes at lines 163 and 168 and read back at lines 174 and 179. In `S_ADDR`, after bits have been shifted in, `ctrl.device_addr = engine.sreg(7 downto 1)` at line 402 and the additional `ctrl.hide_read` condition at lines 403-406 decide whether the engine enters `S_RESP` or returns to `S_IDLE`. Integrity is established because this configuration determines which addressed transfers the module will answer.

conceptual assets.concept: Sampling schedule and detected serial bus events
conceptual assets.reasoning: `twd_sda_i` and `twd_scl_i` are sampled into history registers at lines 311-312. `ctrl.fsel` selects the sampling tap for `smp.clk_en` at line 329; with enable and `smp.clk_en`, the synchronizer advances sample history and asserts `smp.valid` at lines 315-319; bus_event then computes `smp.scl_rise`, `smp.scl_fall`, `smp.start` and `smp.stop` at lines 344-347. The engine uses these events to start, stop, shift, acknowledge and read at lines 381, 389, 397, 401, 411, 423, 427, 438, 448, 455, 467, 473 and 477, so integrity of the timing and event decisions is established; availability is established when enabled sampling pulses occur.

conceptual assets.concept: Active transfer sequencing state and direction/ack decisions
conceptual assets.reasoning: `engine.state` steps through the transfer phases at lines 382, 390, 392, 398, 400, 404, 406, 422, 424, 435, 437, 441, 444, 466, 469 and 487. `engine.cmd <= engine.sreg(0);` (line 420) selects receive versus transmit behavior, and `engine.ack <= smp.sda;` (line 474) controls whether a transmit sequence returns to `S_RTX` at lines 468-469. Integrity is established because these stored decisions govern RX writes, TX reads, SDA driving and busy reporting (lines 443, 454, 478 and 494).

Incoming serial bits are shifted into `engine.sreg` on `smp.scl_rise` at lines 412-413 and 449-450. The stored byte is then used for address comparison at line 402, command extraction at line 420, and RX-buffer write data via `rx_fifo.wdata <= engine.sreg;` (line 282) when `engine.wr_we` is asserted at line 443. Integrity is established because a corrupted byte changes address matching, transfer direction and received-data content; availability is established because the byte is accumulated across sampled clock edges.

conceptual assets.concept: Selected transmit byte and empty-buffer fallback byte
conceptual assets.reasoning: `tx_dummy <= tx_fifo.rdata;` at line 242 keeps the last TX-buffer byte that was actually consumed. `engine.rdata` selects the next response byte from `tx_fifo.rdata`, `tx_dummy`, or all ones at lines 250-252; that selected value is loaded into the transmit path at line 429 and driven externally through `twd_sda_o <= engine.dout;` at line 454. Integrity is established because this path defines the exact byte delivered on the serial output; availability is independently established for the fallback case when `tx_fifo.avail = '0'` and `ctrl.tx_dummy_en = '1'`.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt qualification settings and interrupt request
conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl.irq_rx_avail`, `ctrl.irq_rx_full` and `ctrl.irq_tx_empty` are stored at lines 164-166 and read back at lines 175-177. `irq_o` is then generated as `ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_avail and rx_fifo.avail) or (ctrl.irq_rx_full and (not rx_fifo.free)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_empty and (not tx_fifo.avail)))` at lines 293-296. Integrity is established because the reported interrupt request must match the configured conditions; availability is established whenever enable and a selected condition hold.
